findings.reason: the harness-ownership filter §3 adds ("a session is continued only by the harness that captured it") should be a filter inside `resolve_session`'s source chain, not a parallel resolver, or the two readers will drift exactly where §3's cross-harness falsifier looks.
findings.text: `_current_harness_session` re-resolves a run's session beside `resumption.resolve_session` but its fallback reads a single `observe_log(..., log_path=record["log_path"])` (line 11586) instead of the newest-first stream set `resumption._stream_session` uses; `_stream_session` was written precisely because a run that resumed or changed lane writes its id to a newer stream, so the owner's read and this second read can disagree about the same run

findings.reason: the plan's §3 measure is that capture stops reading as a member write; leaving a member-named alias over a run-only function is the backwards-compatibility shim the repo bans, and the honest change is to rename the four call sites to `capture_run_session` and drop the alias.
findings.text: `_capture_member_session` forwards unconditionally to `capture_run_session` and nothing else ("Compatibility entry point for promotion; capture writes only the run"), is called from four sites (`dispatch.py:11091`, `promotion.py:5341,8146,8656`) and re-exported through `reckon/crew.py:159`, and keeps the name of the member contract §3 retired

findings.reason: §2 introduced the dispatch resolver instead of extending the recovery owner (recovery.py:897 predates it), so the two can compute different task identities for one re-review and the re-review would then continue or miss the earlier review's session depending on which surface is asked.
findings.text: `_reviewed_run_id(source, records)` and `recovery._resolved_reviewed_run_id(record, project)` (reckon/crew/recovery.py:897) are two implementations of "a review node's id maps to the reviewed run id": dispatch matches within the caller's `committed_runs + live_pointers` and picks the newest by timestamp, recovery matches within `list_live()` only and falls back to the raw source; both are reachable for the same review record, and §2's session-continuation key `("review", project, reviewed_run_id)` is built from the dispatch copy while the review store is read through the recovery copy

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — `_current_harness_session` implements a second, weaker session reader beside the `resumption.resolve_session` owner the plan routes the rest of the lookup through.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — `dispatch._reviewed_run_id` is a second reviewed-run-id resolver beside the existing `recovery._resolved_reviewed_run_id`, which the §1 reuse map never named and which §2's task key does not extend.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §1 is a falsifier-gated 34-row reuse map (`~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/ship-s19-20260922/session-carry-sites.md`) that names the review reflex, `resolve_session` as the session store (row E1), the argv-composition sites (A1–A8) and the roster-write sites (B1–B6), so the plan searched before proposing; the gap it did not name is reported under `duplicate_owner`, not as a missed search for a session-carry site.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `_capture_member_session` is a one-line compatibility alias over `capture_run_session` with no behaviour behind it, named for the member contract §3 exists to retire.
